objective.statement: Read a short melody and answer questions about what you see and what it means.
successCriteria: I can find the key, the time signature and the tempo word.
I can name a note and an interval above the tonic.
I can say what the dynamic and articulation marks ask the player to do.

explanation.text: Reading music means using everything you know at once. Work through a melody with a checklist: the clef, the key signature, the time signature, the tempo word, the dynamic marks, and then the notes, rests and signs bar by bar.

music.textAlternative: A four-bar melody in G major, 4/4, marked Andante and mf. Bar 1: G, A, B (marked x, staccato), D. Bar 2: E minim, D minim. Bar 3: B, G, A, then a crotchet rest. Bar 4: G semibreve with a pause.

explanation.caption: An original melody: G major, 4/4, Andante, mf. Bar 1 has a staccato note marked x, bar 3 ends with a rest, and bar 4 has a pause.

explanation.text: Here the key signature has one sharp, so the key is G major and the tonic is G. The time signature 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. Andante tells you to go at a walking pace, and mf means moderately loud.
The note marked x is B. It is a 3rd above the tonic G, because G A B counts as three. It has a dot, so it is played staccato: short and detached.
Take it one bar at a time. If a question asks about 'the highest note', look at every bar before you answer.

music.textAlternative: A four-bar melody in G major, 4/4, marked Andante and mf. Bar 1: G, A, B (marked x, staccato), D. Bar 2: E minim, D minim. Bar 3: B, G, A, then a crotchet rest. Bar 4: G semibreve with a pause.

steps: Press Play all and follow the notes along the stave.
Find the key signature, the time signature and the tempo word before you start.
Find the note marked x, name it, and say what the dot over it asks the player to do.
Spot the rest at the end of bar 3 and the pause sign in bar 4.
